title: Deeper/broader new native DWG and DXF peer-route screen
scope: Search for additional open-source DWG/DXF implementations not yet represented in the parity plan
Classify declared version and entity coverage separately from verified operation-level evidence
Determine whether any new route can provide independent 2D reader evidence or ACIS/AcDs semantics
Refine the optional composed comparator checkpoint without expanding per-slice validation

method.kind: Read-only review of public primary-source repositories and package metadata, reconciled with the local plan
method.limitations: Capability statements, package metadata, and changelogs are not runtime conformance. ezdwg 0.16.3 source-distribution-to-Git-commit correspondence and parser-lineage independence were not established. No peer artifacts were installed or executed.

sources.revision: Mutable main reviewed 2026-10-17; Cargo workspace reports version 0.16.3
sources.observed: The README advertises a Rust-core native DWG reader across AC1012-AC1032 and a native AC1015 writer. It documents experimental AC1012/AC1014 support, lists a limited high-level entity surface, says AC1021/AC1024/AC1027/AC1032 native decoding is regression-tested for only a small core entity set, and calls some modern style/layer resolution best-effort. It states that DWG-to-DXF uses ezdxf and the native writer is AC1015-only/subset.

The source distribution is available with SHA-256 77978afa63fdcc61a18abbd581b9bb1cdac09e5a1747840bb689fbd9771b230c. This provides an immutable package candidate, but the metadata does not establish a matching Git source commit. Platform wheels have separate digests and must be treated as distinct artifacts.

The changelog documents recent work on version-specific readers, writer behavior, entity handling, and checks against ODA and paired samples. These are project-reported implementation/test activities, not independently reproduced conformance results.

The README describes a portable .NET DWG reader/writer based on the ODA specification and lists .NET 7/PowerShell build prerequisites. The reviewed repository page exposes no release and the README does not identify version coverage, entity coverage, or a qualification corpus.

sources.revision: Mutable main reviewed 2026-10-17; last shown NuGet release 0.8.4 dated 2024-06-13
sources.observed: The project documents ASCII/Binary DXF and DXB routes, advertises R10-R2014 completeness with named entity exclusions, while NuGet describes AutoCAD versions through R2018. Its README warns that AutoCAD may reject R13 output and multiple entity writers including 3DSOLID/BODY/REGION.

This supplies an exact package version for a possible optional DXF structure comparator; its version claim does not resolve the repository README's narrower R10-R2014 per-entity status wording or establish native consumer acceptance.

The existing peer matrix already separates DWG parsing, DXF parsing/writing, projection, carrier retention, semantic solid validation, and native acceptance. The new candidate rows fit the existing composed external comparator checkpoint; no local source-confirmed defect was established.

assessment.ezdwg: Potential additional DWG reader evidence for precisely covered 2D entity/version rows only, pending artifact/source reconciliation, lineage audit, and a pinned execution. Its DXF writer is ezdxf-derived and its native DWG writer is AC1015/subset-only.
assessment.ixmiliaDwg: Discovery-only until source inspection establishes exact versions, entities, and reproducible tests; do not count it in the current comparator denominator.
assessment.ixmiliaDxf: Optional ASCII/Binary/DXB structural comparator at an exact package version; its self-described entity/version coverage and AutoCAD caveats prevent broad parity or 3D claims.
assessment.threeDSemantics: No reviewed source establishes ACIS/AcDs payload decoding into complete B-rep semantics or native CAD acceptance. Keep all existing external semantic gates unchanged.
assessment.implementationSpeed: Keep peer install/build/run out of the per-slice loop. If useful, perform one small scratch-generated, source-manifest comparison at the existing composed checkpoint and record each parser/writer operation independently.
